title: AAA User Provisioning - API response time
description: How long airtel-aaa-user-provisioning-service takes to answer, per REST API: the distribution every individual request falls into, from the http_server_requests histogram Spring Boot publishes, and the individual slow requests the service records itself. Grouped by the `api` tag the endpoint catalog adds. See monitoring/RESPONSE-TIME.md.

list.name: threshold
list.label: Slow at
list.description: What counts as slow on the "slower than threshold" panels. The values are the histogram bucket boundaries from management.metrics.distribution.slo - a boundary that is not a bucket has nothing to count, so keep this list in step with that one.

panels.title: Response time over the selected time range
Median (p50)
panels.description: The response time half the requests in this range came in under, read off the http_server_requests histogram buckets. This is the typical request - it moves when the whole service slows down, and barely notices a handful of slow calls.

panels.title: p95
panels.description: 19 requests in 20 were faster than this. The first number to look at when somebody reports the service being slow: an average can hide a slow tail, a p95 cannot.

panels.title: p99
panels.description: 99 requests in 100 were faster than this. Estimated from the histogram buckets, so it is only as precise as the two buckets it falls between - past the 10s bucket there is nothing left to interpolate and it reads 10s.

panels.title: Slowest single request
panels.description: The slowest individual request any of the selected APIs served in this range - an actual request's actual duration, not an estimate. It comes from the timer's own max, which Micrometer keeps over a rolling two-minute window, so a spike shorter than that window is still caught here.

panels.title: Slower than threshold
panels.description: How many individual requests took longer than the threshold picked at the top of the dashboard, over this range. Counted by subtracting the histogram bucket at that boundary from the total, so it is exact rather than interpolated.

panels.title: Share slower than threshold
panels.description: The same requests as a share of all of them. 1% amber and 5% red are display cues only - no API here has a latency budget and nothing alerts on this.

panels.title: Response time by API
panels.description: One row per API in the catalog, over the dashboard's time range. The percentiles are estimated from the histogram buckets; Slowest and Avg are exact, being the timer's own max and its own sum over its own count. Sorted by p95 so the slow API comes to the top. An API nobody called shows 0 requests and leaves every timing column blank - no requests means no response time, and a 0 there would read as instant. The amber and red cues are display thresholds (1s / 3s), not per-API budgets.

targets.expr: sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range])) or sum by (api) (0 * api_endpoint_info{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"})

sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range])) / sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))

sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range])) - sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api", le="$threshold"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Distribution of individual response times
panels.description: Every individual request in the range, dropped into the histogram bucket it fell into: one column per time step, one row per bucket, coloured by how many requests landed there. This is the closest Prometheus gets to plotting each request - a band that sits low with nothing above it is a service answering consistently, and a second band appearing higher up is a slow path that a percentile would only average away. Rows are the buckets from management.metrics.distribution.slo; a request slower than the last one is counted in the +Inf row.

panels.title: p95 response time by API
panels.description: Each API's 95th percentile over the dashboard's time range, worst first. An API with no traffic in the range is absent rather than zero - it has no response time to show.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (api, le) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))) * on (api) group_left(title) max by (api, title) (api_endpoint_info{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"})

panels.title: p95 response time by API
panels.description: Each API's 95th percentile, one point per step of the chart. This is the panel that answers "when did it get slow, and which API was it". A line that is missing is an API that took no traffic in that step.

panels.title: p99 response time by API
panels.description: The same, at the 99th percentile - the slow tail. It is noisier than p95 by nature: at low traffic a single slow request is 1% of the requests.

panels.title: Slowest request by API
panels.description: The duration of the slowest individual request each API served, as the timer itself recorded it. Micrometer decays this max over a rolling two-minute window, so the line falls back on its own once the slow request ages out - a step down is not a recovery, and the height of the peak is the real number to read.

panels.title: Requests slower than the threshold, by API
panels.description: How many individual requests crossed the threshold picked at the top, per step of the chart. Stacked, so the height is every slow request in the service and the bands are which APIs they belong to.

targets.expr: sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by (api) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api", le="$threshold"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Slow requests recorded by the service
panels.description: Requests the service itself timed at or over monitoring.api.response-time.slow-request-threshold-ms, split by severity. Each one of these was logged at WARN with its exact duration and request identifier, so anything on this chart can be looked up as an individual request in the application log. It is measured across the whole filter chain rather than inside the dispatcher, so it sits a little above the bucket-derived count beside it.

panels.title: Slow requests by API, status and severity
panels.description: The same requests over the whole range, broken down. A slow 200 is the service being slow; a slow 500 is usually a timeout somewhere underneath it, and the endpoint's dependencies are the place to look next.

targets.expr: sum by (api, method, status, severity) (increase(api_slow_requests_total{microservice=~"$microservice", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No slow request in this range

panels.title: Most recent request, by API
panels.description: The response time of the last request each API served before the scrape - one individual request, sampled every scrape interval rather than averaged. It is a sample and not a summary: the requests between two scrapes are not on this chart, which is why the panels above read the distribution instead. Useful on a quiet endpoint, where the last request is most of them, and as a sanity check that an API is answering at all.

options.content:
Prometheus stores the **distribution** of response times, never the individual
requests. To go from a slow patch on these charts to the request that caused it,
the service logs every request it timed at or over the slow threshold:

```
WARN  Slow response time: api=create_user POST /api/user
      status=200 duration_ms=1840 UUID=<request id>
```

- `duration_ms` is that one request's actual response time.
- `UUID` ties the line to the request and response the logging
  interceptor wrote for the same call.

```sh
oc -n airtel-aaa logs deploy/airtel-aaa-user-provisioning-service \
  | grep 'Slow response time'
```

Set `monitoring.api.response-time.log-every-request: true` to get the line for
every request, not just the slow ones. See `monitoring/RESPONSE-TIME.md`.
